help.description: How everything works, in short. Search for a word to find the right part.
help.start.title: Your first download
help.start.body:
Copy a link from pawchive.pw and paste it into the bar at the top of Browse, or press Ctrl+L and paste. A post opens with its files, a creator with their posts.
Pick what you want, check the options in the bar at the bottom and press Download. The download appears in Downloads, where you can follow, pause or cancel it.
help.post.title: Downloading a post
help.post.body:
A post shows every file with a thumbnail. Click files to select them, Shift+Click to select a range, and use the type chips to filter. Files you already have are marked Saved.
The Text tab shows the post's description. Save post text stores it next to the files as content.txt.
help.creator.title: Downloading a creator
help.creator.body:
A creator page loads their posts 50 at a time. Search their posts on the site, limit them by date, or filter loaded posts by title and file type.
With nothing selected, Download all scans the whole creator in the background and starts downloading while it is still scanning. Select posts to download only those.
help.batch.title: Batch queue and URL import
help.batch.body: Batch (Ctrl+Shift+B) takes any number of links: paste them, import a text file, or drag them onto the window. Every creator link becomes a download of that creator; posts from the same creator are grouped into one download.
help.formats.title: Separate files, ZIP and thumbnails
help.formats.body:
Separate files saves each post into its own folder, named by the templates in Settings. ZIP writes one archive per post, with no size limit; Settings can split very large posts into parts.
Thumbnails saves only the previews and post text. It is the fallback for when Pawchive's media servers are down.
help.queue.title: The download queue
help.queue.body:
Downloads run in queue order, up to the number of simultaneous downloads set in Settings. Move a waiting download up or to the top to run it sooner.
Pause keeps partly downloaded files; Resume continues them. Failed files are retried automatically with growing pauses, and you can retry them by hand from the item list.
help.resume.title: Resuming and checksums
help.resume.body: Files are written as .part files and continue where they stopped after a pause, a dropped connection or a restart of the app. Each finished file is checked against the SHA-256 checksum in its Pawchive address, and downloaded again if it does not match.
help.preview.title: Preview-only files
help.preview.body: Pawchive keeps only a preview of some files. The full version is usually offered through a temporary link on the post's page, which the app finds and uses. Settings can save the preview instead, or skip such files.
help.watch.title: Watchlist
help.watch.body: Watch a creator to have the app look for new posts on a schedule. New posts show a badge and a notification. Turn on automatic download per creator to queue new posts as soon as they are found.
help.favorites.title: Favorites
help.favorites.body: The star on a post or creator adds it to Favorites. Add a note, download it again in one click, and export or import the list as a text file with one link per line.
help.naming.title: File and folder names
help.naming.body: Templates in Settings decide where files go inside the download folder, for example Pawchive/{creator}/{published:YYYY-MM-DD} {title}. Every value is cleaned so it is valid on Windows, macOS and Linux and cannot leave the download folder.
help.network.title: Proxy and Tor
help.network.body: Settings, Network can send every request through a proxy (http, https or socks5) or through Tor running on this computer. A speed limit keeps downloads from taking all your bandwidth.
help.tray.title: Tray and background
help.tray.body: Closing the window keeps the app in the tray, where downloads and watchlist checks continue. The tray menu pauses or resumes everything, checks the watchlist and quits. Progress also shows on the taskbar button.
help.polite.title: Why downloads are paced
help.polite.body: Pawchive asks clients for at most five downloads at once and one new request per second. The app follows that, and when the site answers that it is busy, every request waits for as long as it asks. This keeps the site fast for everyone.
help.trouble.title: When something goes wrong
help.trouble.body:
If files fail with HTTP 503 or time out, the media servers are busy: the app retries by itself, or try again later. If nothing loads, check your connection and proxy settings.
The Logs page explains what happened; copy it into a report on GitHub if you need help.
help.privacy.title: Privacy
help.privacy.body: There are no accounts, analytics or tracking. Everything the app remembers stays in its folder on this computer, and you can clear it at any time.

help.search.title: Finding creators
help.search.body:
Type a creator's name (or part of it, their id or their public id) into the link bar and press Enter. The app searches the full list of creators on Pawchive, fetched at most once a day.
Results can be limited to Patreon or Fanbox and sorted by best match, most favorited, recently updated or name. Click one to open their page.
A creator's page shows their other accounts (for example Patreon and Fanbox) under the name.
help.filters.title: Filters and clean names
help.filters.body:
Settings > Filters sets default rules: only posts with certain words, skip posts with others (in the title and tags, or also the text), only the newest posts, only or never certain file types, and file names to skip. Each creator download can change them with its Filters button.
Words match regardless of letter case. Write /.../ for a regular expression, for example /ch(apter)?\s*\d+/.
Post rules apply when downloading all or matching posts of a creator, and to watched creators that have their own filters; posts you pick by hand are never left out.
Settings > File names > Remove from names takes words such as [HD] out of titles and file names.
help.schedule.title: Download window, disk space and power
help.schedule.body:
Settings > Downloads > Download window starts downloads only between two times, for example 01:00 to 07:00. Outside it, a bar at the top says when they start again.
Keep free on the drive makes new downloads wait (instead of failing) when the download drive is nearly full; they continue by themselves once there is room.
Keep the computer awake stops it from sleeping while downloads run.
On the Downloads page, When done can quit the app, sleep or shut down once every download has finished, after a 60 second countdown that can be cancelled. Paused downloads never count as finished.

help.sites.title: Pawchive, Kemono and Coomer
help.sites.body:
Links from pawchive.pw, kemono.cr and coomer.st all work the same way (old kemono.su and coomer.su links too). Creator search and Recent posts have a site switch.
The {site} name token puts each site's downloads in its own folder.
When a site's media servers do not answer, a bar at the top says so and can switch to saving thumbnails instead; files are tried again later by themselves.
help.outside.title: Mega, Google Drive and other hosts
help.outside.body:
Turn on Settings > Downloads > Download outside links (or the Outside links box when downloading) and the files posts share on Mega, Google Drive, Dropbox, Pixeldrain, GoFile, MediaFire and direct links are downloaded into a Links folder in the post.
Mega files are decrypted on this computer with the key in the link; the key is never sent anywhere.
Each link in a post's Links tab also has its own download button.
Settings > Downloads > Unpack ZIP archives unpacks ZIPs next to themselves, trying the passwords the post mentions.
help.library.title: Statistics and missing files
help.library.body:
The Statistics page counts everything you have downloaded: files, size, posts and creators, the last twelve months, your most downloaded creators and files by kind.
Check now looks for downloaded files that were deleted or moved since. Download them again fetches only those files (the rest are still known); Only forget them lets the next download of those posts fetch them.
Links to Mega, Google Drive and other hosts found in a post are listed on its Links tab and saved to links.txt with any archive passwords.
help.gallery.title: The Library
help.gallery.body:
Library shows the images and videos the app downloaded, by creator and post, straight from your disk: no site and no network needed. Search, show only images or videos, and pick the tile size.
It also shows images and videos already in your download folders that the app has no record of (saved by another install, the browser extension, or before the history was cleared), placed by their folder names.
Click a file to look at it: Left and Right move, Space starts a slideshow (or pauses a video), the wheel or + and - zoom, a double click shows the actual size, and F goes full screen. Videos play with seeking, and play muted when you point at their tile.
Thumbnails are made once and kept in the app's data folder. Files deleted or moved since are left out and counted, and Statistics can fetch them again.
In Browse, videos from the site play in the viewer too, with the play button on their tile.
help.portable.title: Portable mode and backups
help.portable.body:
With a folder named data next to the program (the portable zip has one), settings, library and logs stay in that folder, so the app can run from a USB stick. About shows Portable when it is on.
Settings > Data > Backup saves your settings, watchlist, favorites and history in one file; Restore adds what is missing on another computer.
help.bridge.title: The browser extension
help.bridge.body:
Settings > Browser extension lets the Pawchive Downloader extension send downloads here. Turn it on, press Pair a browser and enter the six-digit code in the extension's settings within two minutes; the app notices the new browser by itself.
Each paired browser is listed by name, with a green Connected light while it is running. It only listens on this computer, web pages cannot use it, and each paired browser can be removed again (unpairing in the extension removes it here too).
